question.text: A Cat III AIF launched by Ms. Radhika Rao has the following investor profile. Which of the following BREACHES SEBI (AIF) Regulations? (Corpus: INR 22 crore; 20 non-accredited investors.)

answer.text: One employee of the manager commits INR 30 lakh
One non-accredited HNI commits INR 50 lakh
One accredited investor commits INR 5 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Minimum investment per investor in an AIF is INR 1 crore (for non-employees/non-accredited). Employees and directors of the manager can invest a minimum of INR 25 lakh. Accredited investors have a lower threshold under AI framework. A non-accredited HNI committing only INR 50 lakh violates the INR 1 crore minimum. The Trap: Option A matches the INR 1 crore floor exactly — compliant. Option B is INR 30 lakh by an employee — above the INR 25 lakh employee floor, compliant. Option D is an accredited investor — the sub-INR 1 crore floor doesn't apply. Only C breaches. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C, XIX-D all test min ticket. XXI-A / XXI-B PMS has INR 50 lakh minimum — easy to confuse. Manager's Pro-Tip: Run a 'ticket-size validation' script in your subscription system: flag any non-AI, non-employee commitment below INR 1 crore BEFORE signing the contribution agreement. Fixing after allotment is painful.
